key_insight: CQMOM captures coupled size, shape, and velocity distributions of oblate spheroidal particles at over 60× lower cost than a single Monte Carlo realization.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports efficient modeling of non-spherical particle transport, breakage, and classification in industrial processes.
method: Represent a five-dimensional size–aspect-ratio–velocity phase space using conditional quadrature.
Assume particles continuously adopt their drag-maximizing orientation.
Apply Strang splitting to continuous and discontinuous moment-transport operators.
evidence_signal: Across Monte Carlo comparisons involving drag, breakage, recoil, and attrition at different Stokes numbers, two nodes per coordinate reproduce particle number and mean geometry within statistical uncertainty and velocity statistics within 7%.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the drag-maximizing orientation assumption, while conditional velocity quadrature is the main source of remaining numerical deviations.
paper_title: A conditional quadrature method of moments for populations of oblate spheroidal particles
